CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with past medical history of rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for her annual exam. She reports good adherence to exercise regimen including walking, yoga, and running. She denies any joint pain, stiffness, or rheumatoid arthritis flare-ups over the past year and continues methotrexate once weekly without side effects. Regarding atrial fibrillation, she reports continued palpitations with most recent episode approximately one week ago, typically triggered by stress. She has attempted meditation and exercise to manage stress with limited benefit. An event monitor was performed last month. For her reflux, she has made dietary modifications including eliminating soda and continues protonix with good response, reporting no flare-ups in over 5 months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for palpitations and nasal congestion related to allergies. Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

- Rheumatoid arthritis
- Atrial fibrillation
- Reflux

MEDICATIONS
- Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
- Protonix 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES

Not documented.

Patient exercises regularly with walking, yoga, and running. Uses meditation for stress management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Heart rate well controlled and regular. Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated on cardiac examination, regular rate and rhythm. Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally. Musculoskeletal: Right elbow with erythema, edema, and tenderness to palpation. Extremities: No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS
Event monitor: Demonstrates paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses, patient going in and out of normal sinus rhythm. Autoimmune panel: Well controlled on current methotrexate therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Stable on current therapy. Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill provided. Rheumatology referral as needed.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Paroxysmal episodes with stress-induced exacerbations. Refer to cardiology for evaluation for cardiac ablation to maintain normal sinus rhythm.
3. Reflux: Well controlled on current regimen. Continue protonix 40 mg daily. Continue dietary modifications avoiding coffee and spicy foods.
